display.purpose: Hero headline only. One use per page.

label.purpose: Buttons, form labels, table headers, micro-copy.

mono.purpose: Code, prop tables, keyboard shortcuts, install commands.

shadows.name: shadow-xs
shadows.purpose: Resting elevation on outline buttons and inputs. Barely-there.

shadows.name: shadow-md
shadows.purpose: Popovers, the action dock when active.

shadows.name: shadow-card-hover
shadows.purpose: Feature card on hover. Warm-tinted, never pure black.

shadows.name: shadow-dark-md
shadows.purpose: Dark-mode equivalent of shadow-md. Pure black is acceptable in dark mode.

motion.name: ease-out-quart
motion.purpose: Default easing for state transitions and hovers. Exponential ease-out, no bounce.

motion.name: ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: Stronger ease-out for entering elements (action dock slide-in, popover entrance).

motion.name: duration-fast
motion.purpose: Hover state changes within the DataGrid (row hover wash).

motion.name: duration-normal
motion.purpose: Button hover / press transitions, focus ring fade-in.

motion.name: duration-slow
motion.purpose: Card hover lift, larger spatial transitions.

narrative.overview: A workshop after hours: a warm task lamp pooling amber light over a steel workbench, precision tools laid out, the rest of the room receding into deep dusk. The brand surface is the warm task light — parchment cream in day, near-black with a warm tilt at night, copper as the ambient accent. The data surface is the steel — calmer, cooler, with a workshop-blue that carries through tables, charts, and selection states. Two color climates, one workshop. The warmth invites the developer in; the cool precision is what they came to use. The voice is a senior engineer demoing to a peer — warm, direct, technically dense, never hyped.
keyCharacteristics: Warm copper as the brand voice; cool steel-blue as the data voice. The two never fight on the same surface.
Dark mode is the default. Both themes are first-class — neither is an afterthought.
Geometric sans (Geist) for everything. No serif. No display font. Hierarchy through weight + size + tracking, not family.
Engineering-craft references: Linear, Raycast, Vercel for confidence; Resend, Cal.com for warmth.
Above-the-fold artifact is a real, fully interactive DataGrid — not a screenshot, not a hero metric.

rules.name: The Workshop Voltage Rule
rules.body: Workshop Steel and Workshop Twilight are forbidden on the marketing surface (hero, feature cards, nav, footer, CTAs). They live exclusively inside the DataGrid and adjacent data UI. The page is warm; the tool is cool.

rules.name: The One Glow Rule
rules.body: Forge Copper appears on no more than ~10% of any given marketing screen. Its rarity is the point.

rules.name: The Tinted-Neutral Rule
rules.body: Every neutral carries a warm hue tilt (chroma 0.005–0.025). Pure-gray neutrals are forbidden.

rules.name: The No-Caps Rule
rules.body: Section headers, button labels, and tabs are sentence-case. UPPERCASE LABELS are forbidden — they are the most reliable signal of generic SaaS templates.

rules.name: The Tabular Numerals Rule
rules.body: Inside the DataGrid, every numeric cell must enable tabular-numerals (font-feature-settings: 'tnum' 1). Numbers must align column-down, every digit.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: No serif. No second sans. No script. The whole system is one geometric sans family. Variety comes from weight (400, 500, 600) and size, not from typeface contrast.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Cards, sections, and tables sit flat on the surface. Shadows appear only as a response to state or to indicate genuine floating (popover, tooltip, dropdown).

rules.name: The Warm-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Light-mode shadows carry the brand warm hue (hsl(28 18% 25%) at 9–18% opacity). Pure-black shadows on warm parchment read as dirty smudges, not depth.

rules.name: Modal As Last Resort
rules.body: Modals are usually laziness. Exhaust inline editing, popovers, and progressive-disclosure alternatives first.

dos: Do keep the marketing surface warm (parchment + copper) and the DataGrid surface cool-tinted (steel for selection/data accents, twilight for dark-mode panels).
Do use Geist Sans + Geist Mono only. One family for type, period.
Do tilt every neutral toward the brand warm hue. Chroma 0.005–0.025, never 0.
Do put a real, fully interactive DataGrid above the fold on the showcase. The component IS the pitch.
Do enable tabular numerals (font-feature-settings: 'tnum' 1) in every numeric DataGrid cell.
Do honor prefers-reduced-motion: decorative animations shorten or disable; functional state transitions remain.
Do ship both dark and light themes. Dark is the default; light must be equally polished, not an afterthought.
donts: Don't put Workshop Steel or Workshop Twilight on the marketing surface. That collapses the dual-register story into generic enterprise admin.
Don't use gradient text. Delete the .gradient-text utility from index.css.
Don't use glassmorphism. Delete the .glass-panel utility.
Don't ship UPPERCASE LABELS or tracking-wide small-cap section headers.
Don't ship pure black (#000) or pure white (#fff) anywhere.
Don't ship pure-gray borders, surfaces, or text.
Don't ship a 3-column 6-card identical-icon feature grid.
Don't ship hero-metric template (10M+ rows, <1ms render). Show metrics by demonstrating, not announcing.
Don't ship gradient buttons, glowing buttons, or animated borders.
Don't ship a 'Trusted by' logo strip.
Don't ship side-stripe colored borders >1px on cards or callouts. The single permitted left-stripe is the 2px Workshop Steel selected-row indicator inside the DataGrid.
Don't ship border-radius greater than 14px on any element except a circular avatar.
Don't ship modals as a first thought.
Don't introduce a serif. Merriweather has been removed on purpose; do not re-add it.
Don't introduce a display font. Geist Sans at 600 weight handles all display needs.
